worked_solution:
Isolating the quadratic term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-6)^{2}+4 & \ge 11 \\ (x-6)^{2} & \ge 7.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the square root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(x-6)^{2}} & \ge \sqrt{7} \\ |x-6| & \ge \sqrt{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
x-6\ge \sqrt{7}\,\text{or}\,x-6\le -\sqrt{7}
$$

We can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}x-6 & \ge \sqrt{7} &  &  & x-6 & \le -\sqrt{7} \\ x & \ge \sqrt{7}+6 &  &  & x & \le -\sqrt{7}+6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
x\le -\sqrt{7}+6\,\text{or}\,x\ge \sqrt{7}+6.
$$
